scale.meaning: mean(predicted 24-bar RV) / mean(realised 24-bar RV) over the fit window. Divide the raw forecast by this to remove the measured under-dispersion. OUR correction, not the model output.

isotonic.interp: numpy.interp, clipped at the end knots
isotonic.meaning: monotone recalibration of p_vol_amp. OUR correction, not the model output. Fitted once on the fit_window rows above.

fit_window_diagnostics.note: IN-SAMPLE for the calibration; the out-of-sample check is below.

out_of_sample_check.protocol: isotonic fitted on the first half of the fit window, scored on the second

output_clip.reason: The top isotonic knot maps to exactly 1.0 but is supported by a SINGLE fit-window row (p_raw>=0.9667: n=1, 1/1 amplified), so the frozen map could serve a probability of 1.000 -- a claim of certainty from one observation. The output is clipped to [1/(n+1), 1-1/(n+1)] with n=519, the finest resolution a sample of that size can justify. This is a SUPPORT bound, not a tuning knob: it is monotone, so it cannot change the ranking or the AUC, only the extremity of the levels. Added 2026-08-04 after a live call emitted 1.000; the isotonic knots themselves are UNCHANGED.
